text:
alex: heads up — seeing a new cluster spike of NVIDIA Xid errors in eu-west1 today, mostly Xid 31 and some 48s. Impacting ~6 A100 nodes across two autoscale groups. :rotating_light:
maya: ugh. Any pattern on workloads or models?
ajex: (typo) alex: meant to add — correlated with long-chat workloads (512+ tokens) and continuous batching on midsize gpt-like models. Also a couple runs from nightly quantize-eval.
maya: can you paste the dmesg / nvidia-smi output you captured?
alex: pasted logs below — truncated. looks like nvml reset attempts, then Xid 31.
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 31, PID=14422, GPU=0, Channel 00000080, irq 32
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.000000] nvidia-mig: failed to enable profile
[ 12346.100000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 48, PID=14425, GPU=0, Channel 00000040
```
jamie: Xid 31 = GPU page fault/recovery often tied to ECC or kernel/driver mismatch, but on A100 it's frequently workload (memory pressure) + long sustained kernel time. Xid 48 points to GPU reset failure.
raj: region note — these nodes are in eu-west1-b and are on host kernel 5.15 + driver 525. Yes that combo is on our allowed matrix but there was a recent infra upgrade to cudnn 9.1 last week.
maya: good detail. Any ECC events? nvmlECC?
alex: ECC counters show single-bit corrected errors rose shortly before the Xid 31s on 4 of the 6 nodes. Snapshot: "corrected_ecc": ["sbe": 120 -> 410 over 2h]
jamie: that smells like flaky memory under load. Could be thermal or bad DIMM region on GPU.
raj: are the nodes colocated on same rack/power feed? Might be power/temperature.
alex: two nodes share a PSU rack, two are spread. Temperature logs show GPU temps ~78-82C during jobs — within spec but high for sustained runs.
maya: steps? Suggest temporary mitigations: 1) drain affected nodes 2) reduce batch sizes / force single-stream for critical workloads 3) add Xid-based alerting rule 4) collect full NVidia support bundle + open ticket.
jamie: agree. Also try toggling exclusive process mode off/on? sometimes context switching plus multi-stream confuses driver. But that's a bit ad-hoc.
raj: I'll take the drain/replace for the 2 nodes in the same PSU rack. alex — can you collect the full driver logs and socat the nvml dumps to S3?
alex: on it. Will run: 
```bash
sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,PERF,ERRS > /tmp/gpu-diagnostics-1745003210.txt
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-1745003210.txt
# nv-support-bundle (internal tool)
nv-support-bundle --output /tmp/nv-support-1745003210.tar.gz --include /proc/driver/nvidia
```
and then `aws s3 cp /tmp/nv-support-1745003210.tar.gz s3://redwood-infra/gpu-support/`
maya: tagging this P1 for fleet stability. infra-bot will post the drain ticket. :exclamation:
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-6721 and started a node drain for autoscale-group eu-west1-a-mlpool (2 nodes).
alex: uploaded logs to s3://redwood-infra/gpu-support/1745003210/ — link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-infra/gpu-support/1745003210/nv-support-1745003210.tar.gz
jamie: I'll run a synthetic stress to try to reproduce: multi-stream 8x with seq_len=1024 and batch=4, plus KV cache stress. If we can reproduce we can test lowering prefetch/batch config.
raj: also worth noting: our new autoscaler launched some newer A100s with slightly different microcode, maybe mismatch. Can we compare firmware versions?
alex: firmware on bad GPUs: GPU 0 fw 1.2.3, GPU 1 fw 1.2.3, good node fw 1.2.1. So there is variation.
maya: file a support case with NVIDIA including firmware diffs + ECC counts. Meanwhile schedule replace/retag for GPUs hitting >300 corrected ECC in 24h.
jamie: quick triage notes for the ticket: Xid 31 correlated with rising corrected ECC -> memory subsystem stressed by long-sequence, continuous-batching workloads. Xid 48 occurs during attempted resets. Likely root causes: (a) flaky GPU memory region (b) firmware/driver combo edge-case under high sustained kernels (c) possible rack-level power/thermal contributing factor.
alex: I'll mark INFRA-6721 with logs and proposed mitigations. After drain, we should run a full memtest and push driver rollback on 2 nodes to driver 520 as an experiment.
raj: timeline?
maya: drain started, expected replacement by EOD GMT. jamie will run repro tests in the afternoon. We'll reconvene after results. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — adding a Datadog monitor: metric: cuda.xid.count where xid in [13,31,48,79] -> alert if >3 in 10m per node.
jamie: add runbook snippet: if Xid 31 spikes, immediately tag node, stop workloads, move traffic, collect nvml+ecc, then drain.
raj: good. Follow-up: if NVIDIA confirms hardware defect we'll replace and RMA the lot for that rack.
maya: great work team. I'll post a short summary to #incidents and notify customer success for any impacted customers. :shipit:
